subject: SOC 2 evidence: log export sampling, geofence redaction & delivery options
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novamed.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: audit@novamed.com
Date: Mon, 1 Feb 2027 10:14:00 +0000
Subject: SOC 2: admin activity logs — export and redaction questions

Sergio,

Hope you’re well. As part of Novamed’s SOC 2 evidence packet we need to collect admin activity / operator logs for a sample window and confirm export/redaction options. Our external auditor has a few specific asks: 

- Can you provide a 24-hour sample export and a separate 7-day aggregated extract?
- What export formats do you support (CSV/JSONL/Parquet)?
- For customers with EU users, how do you handle geofence/redaction for PII? We need to validate no EU-resident PII leaves EU without consent — what redaction or tokenization options exist?
- Timezone normalization: will timestamps be normalized to UTC or sent in original TZ?
- Delivery options: SFTP with signed manifest, presigned S3 URLs, or encrypted bundle via secure upload?
- Can you provide an attested manifest (checksum + HMAC) for the export?
- If we request encryption key handoff, how do you handle KMS/HSM transfer / wrap policies?

Attached is a spreadsheet with the auditor question rows for your reference (SOC2_questions.xlsx). Can you respond with a proposed plan and timeline? We are under a tight audit window — ideally a sample by next week.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Compliance Manager, Novamed Health

---
From: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novamed.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 1 Feb 2027 14:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: SOC 2: admin activity logs — export and redaction questions

Thanks Elena — appreciate the clear list. Looping in Kimberly (platform ops) and Marissa (security/compliance) to scope the technical and legal sides. High-level responses below; I’ll follow with a concrete delivery plan and checklist by EOD tomorrow.

- Sample windows: we can produce a 24-hour raw extract and a 7-day sessionized export.
- Formats: JSONL and Parquet are our standard for telemetry; we can also provide CSV slices for small samples.
- Geofence/redaction: need to confirm policy choices (hash PII, redact with fixed token, or tokenize and store reference map).
- Timezone: we typically normalize to UTC by default but can include original TZ offset in a separate field.
- Delivery: we support SFTP (FTPS), presigned S3 URLs, and SFTP with signed manifest. We can also generate an encrypted tar.gz wrapped with AES256 (customer-provided KMS key/ wrapped key).
- Manifest: yes — we produce a checksum manifest and can HMAC-sign it using an internal signing key; we can also provide signed attestations upon request.

Kimberly/Marissa — can you confirm encryption/wrap options and the preferred redaction approaches for Novamed so I can propose a specific timeline? Elena — if you can confirm whether the auditor requires deterministic sampling by tenant or true random sampling that will determine how we produce the 24-hour sample.

Sergio
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novamed.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 2 Feb 2027 09:27:00 +0000
Subject: Re: SOC 2: admin activity logs — export and redaction questions

Hi all — technical detail from the ops side (attached: export_options_matrix.csv). Key points: 

1) Formats and schemas
- JSONL: event-per-line with full attribute set; primary choice for audit ingestion.
- Parquet: columnar for large windows; we include a manifest with schema v2 and column types.
- CSV: available but flattened and lossy for nested attributes — suitable for small samples only.

2) Encryption and delivery
- At-rest: AES-256 with envelope encryption.
- Transit: SFTP over FTPS or HTTPS presigned S3 links; both supported.
- KMS: We support customer-supplied KMS keys (AWS KMS/EKS envelope) for wrapping the data key. If Novamed cannot supply a KMS key we will use our KMS and produce a signed key-handoff assertion.

3) Manifest / attestation
- We produce SHA256 checksums for each artifact and a manifest.jsonl. Optionally HMAC the manifest using a per-request HMAC key; we can provide the HMAC key thumbprint.

4) Redaction / PII handling
- Options: (A) redact fields (replace with [REDACTED]); (B) deterministic hashing (sha256 with salt) so auditor can demonstrate pseudonymization; (C) tokenization with reversible tokens stored in a secure vault (only on explicit legal agreement).
- Geofence: we can apply a per-record geolocation check and redaction pipeline prior to export. Redaction is irreversible unless tokenization was chosen.

5) Sampling strategies
- Random: uniform random sample (configurable percent).
- Deterministic: hash-based sampling keyed by tenant ID (stable across exports).
- Windowed: take full fidelity for a fixed time window (recommended for 24-hour) and aggregate for the 7-day extract.

If Novamed wants to avoid cross-border transfers, choose option B (hashing) or A (full redaction) and request that we perform export from our EU region (we can route the export job to eu-central-1).

Kimberly Park
Principal Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference

Elena — from a legal/compliance standpoint a couple of asks to close the plan: 

- Please confirm the jurisdictional scope: if the auditor requires that full-fidelity EU-subject PII never leaves EU, we will execute the export from our EU tenancy and use customer-supplied KMS or our EU-local KMS (no key export).
- We will attach an attestation letter indicating the export was produced from eu-central-1 and include the signed manifest.
- For tokenization (reversible) we require a Data Processing Agreement addendum and explicit approval from Novamed’s legal — that slows timeline.
- Timeline: we can provision the job for a 24-hour full-fidelity extract (or a pseudonymized 24-hour sample) within 5 business days after you confirm sampling approach and KMS preferences.

Proposed minimal deliverable for audit: a 24-hour JSONL from EU region with deterministic hashing on PII fields + SHA256 manifest + HMAC signature; delivery via presigned S3 link with 7-day expiration. If Novamed wants private-key handoff for HMAC verification, we can do a KMS-wrapped verification key exchange with an audit log.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Elena — thanks for the patience. Based on the thread above here’s the concrete plan we’ll execute once you confirm: 

1) Scope & sampling
- Deliverable A (by 2027-02-08): 24-hour deterministic-sample export (JSONL) taken from eu-central-1 if you confirm EU-scope. Sampling will be 5% deterministic by tenant id (stable across repeats).
- Deliverable B (by 2027-02-10): 7-day aggregated Parquet export (columns + counts) with UTC-normalized timestamps.

2) PII handling
- Default: deterministic sha256(salt+value) hashing for name/email/phone fields. Salt will be included in the HMAC-covered manifest (not in raw export). If you require irreversible redaction we will redact instead. Tokenization (reversible) available only after DPA addendum.

3) Encryption, manifest & delivery
- Artifacts: data_export_20270208.jsonl.gz (AES-256 envelope), sample_export_manifest.sha256 (SHA256 checksums), manifest.hmac (HMAC-SHA256 over manifest).
- Delivery: presigned S3 URL (7-day expiry) + manifest.hmac delivered over separate channel (SFTP or HubSpot secure note).
- KMS: we can accept a customer KMS key to wrap the data key. If none provided, we will use our EU-local KMS and include the signed key assertion.

4) Attestations & evidence
- We will include a short attestation PDF stating the export region and that redaction/hashing policy was applied.
- We will log the export job id and provide an audit trace link (COMPLIANCE-4821).

Next steps for you: confirm (A) prefer EU-local export? (B) sampling method: deterministic 5% or full 24-hour export? (C) KMS: customer-supplied or Redwood EU KMS?

If you confirm by EOD tomorrow we will schedule the 24-hour sample for 2027-02-08 and share the presigned link + manifests.

Thanks — Sergio
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
